recipes.name: Cheddar Bacon Mac and Cheese
ingredients_raw: 2 cups KRAFT Shredded Sharp Cheddar Cheese, divided
3 slices OSCAR MAYER Center Cut Bacon, cooked, crumbled

steps.text: Gather all ingredients. Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook elbow macaroni in the boiling water, stirring occasionally, until tender yet firm to the bite, about 8 minutes. Drain and keep warm.

At the same time, melt butter in a large saucepan over low heat. Whisk in flour and stir until mixture becomes paste-like and bubbly, about 2 minutes. Gradually whisk in milk and bring to a simmer over medium heat. Cook and stir until the mixture is thick and smooth, 3 to 5 minutes. Stir in 1 1/2 cups Cheddar and cook until melted, about 5 minutes.
Add macaroni and bacon to the saucepan; gently stir to combine with sauce. Add additional milk only if needed to evenly coat the pasta.
Transfer to a 1 1/2-quart casserole dish; sprinkle remaining 1/2 cup Cheddar over top. Bake in the preheated oven until hot and bubbly, about 20 minutes. Serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Cheddar Bacon Mac and Cheese
raw_recipe.description: Add bacon to mac and cheese and take this favorite comfort food to a whole new level. This quick and easy recipe is better than any boxed mix.

review.reviewBody: verry good a good thanksgiving twist

This was my first time making any type of baked Mac and Cheese, and it came out great. Rave reviews from the hubby and kids. The only changes I made to the recipe were: I used 2 cups of evaporated milk instead of regular, added salt & pepper as I was mixing the macaroni and mixture together. I spooned half of the macaroni into the casserole dish and then added a layer of shredded cheese before adding the rest of the macaroni. I topped it off with the layer of cheese as the recipe calls for, but also sprinkled some parmasean cheese and fine bread crumbs. I would NOT skip the bacon - it just took the dish to the next level (I even added extra!) Will make this again real soon!

This was a HUGE hit at a party! I wanted to make something kid friendly,and this was perfect (the adults loved it too...they wound up using it as a chili topper). I had to adjust according to what I had on hand and the amount needed. Here's my alterations: used an entire box (probably about 2.5 or 3 cups) of Vegetable Elbo Macaroni...2 cups of flax milk and about a cup of cream (stirred in the flax milk first)...a litte over 2 bags (so over 4 cups) of shredded cheese (one cheddar, the other a mexican mix)...and about 8 pieces of thick bacon. I also had great wisconsin cheddar so I shredded that on top before popping in the oven. I'll definitely be making this again! Oh, whatever you do, do not skip the bacon. It's the key ingredient. If you do then add seasonings, especially salt.

I Made 3 alterations: 1) I added some fresh minced garlic (2 cloves) and 1 small yellow onion. Sautéed them with a touch of butter and added it into the cheese sauce. 2) used light cream instead of milk. It makes the sauce thicker so i didnt need the flour. 3) I added a tablespoon of the bacon droppings to the cheese sause for a little extra flavor. Heavenly!!

I quadrupled the recipe.
Used light cream instead of milk.
Used 4 cups of max n cheese blend, 2 cups of extra sharp cheddar and 1.5 cups of shredded parmesan cheese in the sauce.
I added 4 tablespoons of bacon grease to the rue. 
I also added a layer of shredded extra sharp in the middle and a layer on top with some parmesan cheese and panko bread crumbs.
Came out rich and delicious!

I sliced bacon in 1 inch pieces and fried until crispy. Pour out all but a tbsp. of bacon fat and created the roux in the frying pan. Used whole milk and some whipping g cream, scraped up all the carmelized sugars left on the pan. Cooked until slightly thickened then added my cheddar. Used rotini pasta. Baked in oven . Wow so good

I added a small tomato chopped up very fine and a dash (or two - depending) of cayenne pepper. I also cooked it much longer (I live at 5000 feet) at 330F for an hour and 15 minutes. I added Panko breadcrumbs to the top after about 30 minutes. Amazing. The tomato disappeared into the dish but it left a very subtle flavor. Give it a try!!!

Best ever! I swapped 1/2c half and half for 1/2c of the milk, because I only had 2% milk. I added 1c or so cheese, swapping 1/2c Monterey Jack. Topped it with panko crumbs mixed with some bacon drippings and Parmesan cheese. Yum! This creamy concoction is a great base for any taste- broccoli, red peppers, onions, lobster or anything you like could be added.

I put 3 tbsps of flour. I was taught equal amounts of flour and butter . I also put 2 cups of elbows and I used a shredded cheese made by Armstrong that had real pieces of bacon in it already so there was no needto cook bacon. Also added some Dan-o's seasoning to the sauce.

I did a few modifications which made it very unhealthy but still awesome! I didn't have elbow on hand so I used gluten free bow tie pasta and, since our family likes a variety of cheeses, I added a few extra. I cut the cheddar in half and added some monterey jack, parmesan, and a dollop of cream cheese in it's place, stirring in a little salt and ground pepper as others recommended. I also cut the milk to 1 1/2 C and added 1/2 C half and half. Because I like to cook gluten free, I used corn starch instead of flour. It was fabulous and I will be making it again! :-)

This is so easy and tasty. I appreciated the fact that the bacon added nice flavor without overpowering the dish. I used a package of cheese ends I got at the deli which was a mish-mash of different cheeses instead of plain cheddar and it worked perfectly. I added all the cheese to the milk mixture and topped the casserole with buttered cracker crumbs as a personal preference. It was creamy and delicious. Added note: This is also a hit made with Johnsonville Breakfast Sausage instead of the bacon.

Fry bacon and remove from the pan, set aside until required. Then in the bacon fat add 1 diced onion fry until al'dente. Then add 1 large freshly chopped tomato and cook for 2 min. Add the bacon into the onion & tomato, some Italian dried herbs mix and cook for 3 - 4 min incorporating all the flavours. Remove from the heat and add this mixture to your white sauce and macoroni. Sprinkle over a mixture of shredded Mature cheddar, Parmesan & some Mozarella cheese, bake in a 190C oven until hot, melting and golden. It's too fabulous. Enjoy.
Never thought such an awesome dish would be soooo easy!

This was pretty good, but I thought it needed a bit more flavor. I used more cheese than called for because it didn't taste very cheesy with 2 cups. After baking, I found it was a little dry, so I’d add more milk to thin out the sauce. A perfect side for smoked ribs.
This is so good I am making it again for Easter.
It’s a great recipe but the sauce is a little bland so I would recommend putting your favourite hot sauce in with it as well to give it a little more flavour and a nice kick.
The cheese sauce aka rue was was not thick so we added more cheese but it is good my mom was glad I made dinner!
I added some Pablo and Frank’s red hot powder on top at the end and chicken breasts. Delicious!!
